project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
A market-driven research project, investment project or combination that gives the Groningen-Emmen region a new economic or green perspective after the end of gas extraction.
The call funds Tracks 1 and 2 of the TJTP (Territorial Just Transition Plan, the EU-approved plan for the region's shift away from gas extraction and fossil industry). Track 1 renews the regional economy and strengthens the knowledge infrastructure. Track 2 transforms industry towards green production by replacing fossil fuels and feedstocks. "Marktgedreven" (market-driven) means private companies take part as project partners and bear at least 20% of the total eligible project costs.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 1-2 · Artikel 2.16.1 Begripsbepalingen; Artikel 2.16.2 Doel subsidie
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 6 · Toelichting, 1. Inhoud regeling

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
Research and innovation, and investments in clean energy, digitalisation, the circular economy and new businesses, all linked to the regional transition plan; linked retraining can be added.
Eligible activities (one or more):
- productive investments by SMEs and large companies; for large companies limited to new establishments, diversification and environmental investments
- research and innovation projects
- investments in digitalisation or robotics
- investments in technology, systems and infrastructure for affordable clean energy, including energy storage and greenhouse-gas reduction
- circular-economy investments
- investments in new businesses, including 'demonstrators at scale' (first commercial applications of innovative technology in the process and manufacturing industry)
- retraining measures linked to the project, as a side activity only
The concrete actions named include system studies of promising options in the energy infrastructure, feasibility or engineering studies for converting industry, renewable energy production, renewable gases and sustainable hydrogen, CCU and CCS (carbon capture and use or storage), and regional and local transport backbones with smart energy systems for industrial clusters.
Excluded: projects that are not market-driven, projects in the form of a financial instrument (loan, guarantee or equity), and requests below EUR 1 million.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 2-3 · Artikel 2.16.4 Subsidiabele activiteiten
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 4 · Artikel 2.16.9 Afwijzingsgronden
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 6-7 and 10 · Toelichting, 1. Inhoud regeling; Toelichting Artikel 2.16.4

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
The economic and social impact on Groningen-Emmen of ending gas extraction in 2022 and of the climate transition, in a region whose economy rests on gas and fossil-based industry.
The need is the region's and its industry's: the projects must come from a concrete demand from business, with entrepreneurs actively involved, according to the SNN page. Projects must fit Track 1 or Track 2 of the TJTP Groningen-Emmen and the RIS3 (the innovation strategy of Northern Netherlands). For infrastructure projects, the applicant must show how the infrastructure adds value to the Groningen-Emmen region.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 6 · Toelichting, 1. Inhoud regeling
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 12-13 · Toelichting criterion A, Spoor 1 and Spoor 2
SNN, Een nieuwe, groene economie · scheme page introduction

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
The research results or realised investments, with contributions to the JTF programme indicators and, for Track 2 investments, a substantiated CO2 reduction.
- Research projects: new knowledge, products or production processes, or significantly improved ones.
- Investment projects: the installed assets, with a business case covering the project and the first two years of operation.
- Track 2 investments: evidence, prepared to a professional standard such as the GHG Protocol or a life-cycle analysis, that the investment is needed for the shift to zero CO2 or reduces CO2 in EU value chains.
- Progress reports for projects longer than 12 months, and a settlement request within four weeks after 29 June 2029.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 1 and 4 · Artikel 2.16.1 (onderzoeksproject); Artikel 2.16.8 Starttermijn en looptijd
JTF Hoofdstuk 1 - publieksversie (11) dd 12 november 2026.pdf · p. 11 · Artikel 1.29 Rapportageverplichtingen
SNN, Een nieuwe, groene economie · Aanvraag voorbereiden (Dit heb je nodig voor je aanvraag)

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Diversification and modernisation of the regional economy, jobs, and CO2 reduction in industry, with the results landing mainly in Groningen-Emmen.
- JTF aim: soften the negative effects of the climate transition on the most affected areas and workers, by limiting job losses and financing diversification and modernisation of the local economy.
- Track 1: new value chains and earnings models, a stronger knowledge infrastructure, a favourable business climate and a stronger competitive position.
- Track 2: direct (scope 1), energy-supplier (scope 2) or value-chain (scope 3) CO2 reduction, or new, greener industrial chains.
- Society: people, planet and profit aspects such as training, jobs for people at a distance from the labour market, energy saving and reduced use of raw materials.
The call sets no numerical targets but scores the contribution to the programme indicators.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 11-13 · Toelichting criterion A (Bijdrage aan doelstellingen), Spoor 1 and Spoor 2
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 15-16 · Toelichting criterion E (Duurzame ontwikkeling en maatschappelijke impact)

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
Results must stay in and benefit the region; subsidised investments must be maintained, normally for five years after the final payment.
- Location of results: if not all activities take place in Groningen-Emmen, the applicant must show that results such as ownership rights or production land there to a significant extent.
- Durability: the subsidy is withdrawn if, within five years of the last payment (three years for SMEs), production capacity is ended or moved, infrastructure ownership changes in a way that gives an undue advantage, or the activity changes substantially.
- Commercial follow-up: research projects must describe the route to market and the follow-up after the subsidy period; investment projects need a business case covering two operational years.
The call sets no replication or standardisation requirement.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 8 · Toelichting, 1. Inhoud regeling (projectresultaten)
JTF Hoofdstuk 1 - publieksversie (11) dd 12 november 2026.pdf · p. 13 · Artikel 1.36 Instandhouding activiteit
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 14 · Toelichting criterion C

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
A single legal entity may apply, but at least one private company must be a project partner bearing at least 20% of eligible costs.
The call sets no minimum or maximum number of partners; its own cost estimate assumes an average of three partners.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 1-2 · Artikel 2.16.1 (marktgedreven); Artikel 2.16.3 Doelgroep
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 8 · Toelichting, 3. Regeldruk

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
Private companies must take an active role; cooperation between companies and knowledge institutions, and with SMEs, is encouraged.
Track 1 research projects should strengthen cooperation between knowledge institutions and business, with special attention to SMEs. Cross-overs between sectors score higher on innovation. Partners need not be located in the region, but the results must land mainly in Groningen province or Emmen municipality. Complementarity, roles and commitment within the consortium are scored under quality.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 1 · Artikel 2.16.2 Doel subsidie
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 8, 13, 15 · Toelichting (projectresultaten; criterion B; criterion D)

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
Private companies must together carry at least 20% of the total eligible costs; research and investment parts have separate caps.
The subsidy and the state-aid ceiling are worked out per beneficiary, so rates may differ between partners. A lead partner (penvoerder) applies on behalf of the partners and receives the decisions and payments for them.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 1 · Artikel 2.16.1 (marktgedreven)
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 8 · Toelichting, 2. Staatssteun
JTF Hoofdstuk 1 - publieksversie (11) dd 12 november 2026.pdf · p. 9 · Artikel 1.23 Beslissing op de aanvraag

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
Any legal entity, a natural person registered in the trade register, or a lead partner applying on behalf of a consortium.
The explanatory note states the target group is not limited by content: any legal or business form, or collaboration, may apply.
cards.sources: JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 2 and 9 · Artikel 2.16.3 Doelgroep; Toelichting Artikel 2.16.3

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Yes, TenneT may apply or lead as a legal entity, provided private companies in the project carry at least 20% of eligible costs.
Whether TenneT, a state-owned company, counts towards that 20% private share is not stated in the regulation; a TenneT-led project should therefore include private industrial partners that bear their own 20%. Applications must first be discussed with the province of Groningen or the municipality of Emmen and with SNN.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 1-2 · Artikel 2.16.1 (marktgedreven); Artikel 2.16.3 Doelgroep
SNN, Een nieuwe, groene economie · Proces, Stap 1

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: Yes. The rules do not stop TenneT from joining as a partner that bears its own costs, though the regulation does not define an unfunded role.
cards.sources: JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 9 · Toelichting Artikel 2.16.3

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes, for research at up to 50% and for investments at up to 30%, but large-company investments are limited and state-aid rules can lower the rate.
- Research activities: up to 50% of eligible costs, at most EUR 4 million per project.
- Investments: up to 30% of eligible costs, at most EUR 10 million per project.
- Large companies such as TenneT: productive investments only for a new establishment (a new company, head office, laboratory, innovation department or site), diversification or environmental investments (investments that reduce environmental damage or promote renewable energy or efficiency).
- State aid: the General Block Exemption Regulation (the EU rules on aid that governments may give without notifying Brussels) is applied per beneficiary, and the lower rate prevails.
TenneT must finance the rest of its costs itself.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 1-3 · Artikel 2.16.1 (milieu-investering); Artikel 2.16.4, lid 4a; Artikel 2.16.7 Hoogte subsidie
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 8 and 10 · Toelichting, 2. Staatssteun; Toelichting Artikel 2.16.4 (vestigingsprojecten)

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
My judgement: TenneT would be most credible as the grid partner in an industry-led project that needs new electricity connections or flexible capacity in an industrial cluster such as Eemshaven or Delfzijl.
The call explicitly covers system studies of the energy infrastructure, investments in systems and infrastructure for clean energy and storage, and regional transport backbones and smart energy systems for industrial clusters. TenneT could contribute system studies, grid-capacity analysis and connection planning for the cluster, which match its Energy boards and Target Grid work, while private companies carry the market-driven 20% and the investments. A research or study work package at 50% would fit TenneT better than investments, which are restricted for large companies.
cards.sources: JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 2-3 and 6-7 · Artikel 2.16.4; Toelichting, 1. Inhoud regeling

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer:
New knowledge or technology is not required in every case: research projects must be innovative, but investment projects are judged on how new they are for the region or the company.
For research and valorisation projects, innovation may come from new technologies or from smartly combining existing ones, or a new application of something existing. For investment-only projects, the call scores how far the investments are integrated into and renew the business process.
cards.sources: JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 13-14 · Toelichting criterion B (Mate van innovativiteit)

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer:
Mainly technology and production processes, together with new value chains, earnings models and business models.
The call names new technology in clusters and companies, digitalisation and robotics, new raw materials with related business models, and new circular value chains.
cards.sources: JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 2-3 and 6 · Artikel 2.16.4, lid 5; Toelichting, 1. Inhoud regeling

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Research, feasibility and engineering studies, demonstration at scale and investment, alone or combined; combining research and investment is not required.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 2-3 · Artikel 2.16.4
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 10 · Toelichting Artikel 2.16.7

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Demonstration is optional; where used, it is at full scale in real operations, such as 'demonstrators at scale' for first commercial use in the process and manufacturing industry, or demonstration projects for access to renewable energy.
cards.sources: JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 2-3 · Artikel 2.16.4, lid 4f and lid 5c, 5l

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer:
Investments are scored on how well they are integrated into existing business processes, and projects must build on the regional industrial ecosystem.
Track 1 projects are assessed on their contribution to chain formation in the sector and their synergy with existing regional companies. Infrastructure projects must show their added value for the region. Activities must not overlap with existing facilities.
cards.sources: JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 12-15 · Toelichting criteria A (Spoor 1 and 2), B (Investeringsprojecten) and D

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer:
Track 2 projects must quantify CO2 reduction; all projects report on the JTF output and result indicators.
For Track 2 investments, the CO2 reduction must be substantiated to a professional standard such as the GHG Protocol or a life-cycle analysis, prepared by an external expert unless the applicant has the expertise in-house. An indicator overview is a required annex.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 12 · Toelichting criterion A, Spoor 2
SNN, Een nieuwe, groene economie · Aanvraag voorbereiden (Dit heb je nodig voor je aanvraag)

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
Between EUR 1 million and EUR 10 million of subsidy per project, or EUR 11 million with linked training measures, from a EUR 70 million budget.
- Total project size: not stated; at the 50% research rate the EUR 1 million minimum corresponds to EUR 2 million of eligible costs, and at the 30% investment rate the EUR 10 million maximum to about EUR 33 million (my calculation)
- Grant request: EUR 1-10 million per project; research part at most EUR 4 million; training at most 10% of the research and investment subsidy, up to EUR 1 million
- Funding form: a share of actual eligible costs; staff costs use simplified cost options or integral cost systems
- Budget: EUR 70 million, of which at most EUR 32 million only for activities under the EU STEP and mid-term review regulations. The explanatory note still mentions EUR 50 million; the article in the 11 June 2026 version says EUR 70 million.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 3-4 · Artikel 2.16.5 Subsidieplafond; Artikel 2.16.7 Hoogte subsidie; Artikel 2.16.9e
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 8 and 10 · Toelichting, 3. Regeldruk; Toelichting Artikel 2.16.6 and 2.16.7

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Rates depend on the activity, and state-aid rules may set lower rates per partner.
- Research activities: up to 50% of eligible costs
- Investments: up to 30% of eligible costs
- Linked training measures: up to 50% of eligible costs
- Co-financing conditions: private companies must bear at least 20% of total eligible costs; any other financing must be shown, with proof or an (uncommitted) term sheet from other financiers
- Evidence required: a state-aid analysis for every partner and work package, and the latest adopted annual accounts
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 1 and 3 · Artikel 2.16.1 (marktgedreven); Artikel 2.16.7 Hoogte subsidie
SNN, Een nieuwe, groene economie · Aanvraag voorbereiden; Veelgestelde vragen (Wat is een steunanalyse?)

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Costs count only after the application is submitted, and staff costs follow fixed or simplified rates.
- Eligible costs: costs incurred after the application, with an exception for preparation costs if the regional opening allows it; VAT only if it cannot be reclaimed
- Caps or mandatory allocations: research subsidy at most EUR 4 million; training at most 10% of the subsidy and EUR 1 million
- Overheads and VAT: staff costs through a fixed hourly rate (EUR 60 per hour under one of the methods) or an approved integral cost system
- Subcontracting or equipment: contracts above EUR 70,000 with one supplier must be shown to be at market price, unless the beneficiary is a contracting authority under the Dutch Procurement Act, which must follow that act
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 3 · Artikel 2.16.7
JTF Hoofdstuk 1 - publieksversie (11) dd 12 november 2026.pdf · pp. 10 and 25 · Artikel 1.26, leden 5-8; Toelichting Artikel 1.11 and 1.12

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
A 10% advance before the start, up to 40% on a motivated request, and further advances up to 80% based on costs paid.
- Payment model: 10% advance on request before activities start; up to 40% if motivated and after a positive risk analysis; further advances on costs incurred and paid, up to 80% in total; up to 100% in exceptional liquidity cases
- Retention or guarantee: no advance is paid if the grant decision has suspensive or resolutive conditions, for example permits still pending
- Financial reporting or audit: the settlement request is due within four weeks after 29 June 2029
cards.sources: JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 4-5 · Artikel 2.16.8; Artikel 2.16.11 Voorschot

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
A mandatory intake talk, then one full application through the JTF web portal; budget is allocated first come, first served.
- Stage 1 — Intake: discuss the draft project plan, in SNN's format, with the province of Groningen or the municipality of Emmen (content) and SNN (subsidy rules), and receive a written reflection. The call gives no separate deadline; allow time before 15 December 2026.
- Stage 2 — Full application: from 14 July 2025, 09:00, until 15 December 2026, before 17:00, through the JTF web portal (jtf-webportal.nl) with eHerkenning level 2+ (the Dutch business login)
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 3 · Artikel 2.16.6 Aanvraagperiode
SNN, Een nieuwe, groene economie · Proces; Aanvraag voorbereiden (Stappenplan)
SNN, Een nieuwe, groene economie · Veelgestelde vragen (Heb ik een eHerkenning nodig?)

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
Projects must start within three months (research) or six months (investments) of the grant and be completed by 29 June 2029.
- Maximum duration: 36 months from the grant, according to the SNN page
- Required start: within three months of the grant for research projects, six months for investment projects
- Eligible-cost period: from submission of the application to the end of the project
- Completion deadline: 29 June 2029; the settlement request within four weeks after that. The minister may extend these terms on request.
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 4 · Artikel 2.16.8 Starttermijn en looptijd
SNN, Een nieuwe, groene economie · Wat zijn de voorwaarden?

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
A decision within 26 weeks of receipt of the application.
- Funding decision: within 26 weeks; SNN checks completeness within one to two weeks of submission
- Conditions before starting: permits not yet granted must be obtained within six months of the grant, as a suspensive condition
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 1 - publieksversie (11) dd 12 november 2026.pdf · p. 9 · Artikel 1.23 Beslissing op de aanvraag
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 4 and 11 · Artikel 2.16.8, lid 2; Toelichting, 1. Compleetheidstoets

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
A long list of documents is needed; SNN first checks completeness.
- Application form: the JTF application form with the project plan in SNN's format
- Budget: the JTF 2021-2027 budget format
- Mandatory annexes: indicator overview; state-aid analysis; permits schedule; for investments, a business case with an operating budget for the project and two operational years; for Track 2 investments, a CO2-reduction substantiation; proof of co-financing or an uncommitted term sheet where relevant; any other subsidy decisions
- Partner documents: signature forms for the lead partner and each partner, proof of signing authority, collaboration agreement where relevant, statements on financial difficulties, SME and linked-enterprise declarations, de minimis declaration where relevant, legal group structure, latest annual accounts, and a bank statement
- Registration: eHerkenning level 2+
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 5 · Artikel 2.16.12 Subsidieaanvraag
SNN, Een nieuwe, groene economie · Aanvraag voorbereiden (Dit heb je nodig voor je aanvraag)

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
An independent expert committee scores five criteria; complete applications above the threshold are funded in order of receipt.
- Evaluation criteria and weighting: contribution to the JTF programme 30 points; technical and social innovation 20; economic and financial prospects 20; quality of the project plan 15; sustainable development and social impact 15
- Thresholds: at least 70 of 100 points, and at least half the points on each criterion
- Ranking rules: first come, first served after a positive assessment and approval by SNN's board
- Budget assessment: SNN checks state aid, the project period, the maximum subsidy and whether financing is complete
cards.sources:
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · p. 4 · Artikel 2.16.10 Beoordelingscriteria
JTF Hoofdstuk 2.16 - publieksversie (3) 11 juni 2026.pdf · pp. 10-11, 16-17 · Toelichting Artikel 2.16.10; 3. Subsidie-technische beoordeling
JTF Hoofdstuk 1 - publieksversie (11) dd 12 november 2026.pdf · p. 9 · Artikel 1.25 Afwijzingsgronden

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Several conditions apply only to particular projects.
- Conditional — permits not yet granted: the subsidy can be granted on condition that all permits are obtained within six months; no advance is paid meanwhile
- Conditional — productive investment by a large company: allowed only as a new establishment, diversification or environmental investment, and the application must show that job losses without the investment would exceed the jobs it creates
- Conditional — new establishment: decisive under criterion A are its strategic value, sustainability, links to regional knowledge infrastructure and long-term embedding
- Exception — training measures: allowed only as a side activity linked to the project, at up to 50% and within 10% of the subsidy
- Recommended: have the state-aid analysis prepared by a specialist
